title: Enthalpy of solution & hydration
examples: How does the lattice energy affect how much salt dissolves?
What is the difference between hydration and solution enthalpy?
Can you explain why some salts are more soluble than others?

explain.say: Today we will look at energy changes when dissolving salts.
The lattice energy is the energy required to break apart the solid crystal.
Hydration enthalpy is the energy released when ions are surrounded by water molecules.
The overall enthalpy of solution is the sum of these two energy changes.
If the released hydration energy is greater than the lattice energy, the salt dissolves well.
In real life, dissolving sugar in water is an example of this process.

faq.q: Does the temperature affect the solubility trend?
faq.a: Generally, for most solids, increasing the temperature increases the solubility. This is because the process becomes less exothermic.
asks: Will solubility always increase with heat?

faq.q: Is the lattice energy the same as the bond energy?
faq.a: No, lattice energy is specific to ionic solids and refers to the energy needed to separate the crystal lattice into gaseous ions. Bond energy is a more general term.
asks: What is the difference between lattice and bond energy?
Can you compare lattice energy to covalent bonding?

faq.q: Does the charge on the ion affect hydration enthalpy?
faq.a: Yes, higher charges lead to stronger interactions with polar water molecules, resulting in a more negative, or larger, hydration enthalpy.
asks: Do ions with higher charges dissolve better?
How does ion charge affect water interaction?

faq.q: If the enthalpy of solution is positive, what does that mean?
faq.a: A positive enthalpy of solution means that energy must be put into the system to break the lattice, and this input energy is greater than the energy released by hydration.
asks: What does a positive ΔHsol indicate?
Does a positive energy change mean it won't dissolve?

faq.q: Are there exceptions to the solubility trend?
faq.a: Yes, some salts exhibit complex behavior where solubility might not increase linearly with temperature. This is due to changes in the structure of the solid or solution.
asks: Are there any salts that behave unusually?
When does solubility stop increasing with heat?

facts: Lattice energy is the energy required to separate one mole of a solid ionic compound into its gaseous ions.
Hydration enthalpy is the energy change when one mole of gaseous ions are dissolved in water to form aqueous ions.
The overall enthalpy of solution is the sum of the lattice enthalpy and the hydration enthalpy.
A more negative enthalpy of solution generally indicates higher solubility.

quiz.say: Which factor primarily determines the energy needed to break the crystal structure?

options.show: The charges and sizes of the ions.
options.say: The charges and sizes of the ions.

quiz.why: The strength of the electrostatic attraction between ions determines the lattice energy.

wrong.0: The color is a visible property and has no bearing on the chemical energy involved.
wrong.2: Temperature affects the kinetic energy but not the fundamental bond strength.
wrong.3: The amount of solvent does not change the inherent energy required to break the solid.

quiz.say: If the hydration energy is very large and negative, what is likely true about the salt?

options.show: The lattice energy must also be very negative.
options.say: The lattice energy must also be very negative.

options.show: The salt will likely have high solubility.
options.say: The salt will likely have high solubility.

options.show: The salt will be difficult to dissolve.
options.say: The salt will be difficult to dissolve.

options.show: The salt must be covalent in nature.
options.say: The salt must be covalent in nature.

quiz.why: A large negative value means a lot of energy is released, which favors dissolution.

wrong.0: Lattice energy is an energy input, making it positive, not negative.
wrong.2: This suggests the energy released is too small to overcome the lattice energy.
wrong.3: Hydration energy specifically relates to ionic interactions with water.

options.show: The magnitude of lattice energy versus hydration energy.
options.say: The magnitude of lattice energy versus hydration energy.

options.show: Only the melting point of the solid.
options.say: Only the melting point of the solid.

options.show: The boiling point of the solution.
options.say: The boiling point of the solution.

options.show: The density of the resulting solution.
options.say: The density of the resulting solution.

quiz.why: Solubility depends on the balance between the energy needed to break the solid and the energy released upon hydration.

wrong.1: The melting point only measures the energy to break the solid, ignoring water interaction.
wrong.2: The boiling point relates to vapor pressure, not the dissolution energy balance.
wrong.3: Density is a measurement of mass per volume and does not predict the energy favorability of dissolution.
